groups.title: Valuation Gap
groups.description: Comparing current market values against historical norms.

metrics.label: Shiller P/E Ratio
metrics.description: indicates the market is highly overvalued from a historical perspective - more than double the long-term average. Change shows the absolute difference from a year ago.
metrics.explanation: Higher values typically indicate greater market overvaluation. A rising trend may suggest growing speculative excess.

metrics.label: Investments in AI
metrics.description: in global corporate AI investment last year, according to Stanford University's AI Index Report 2025.
metrics.disclaimer: This tracks total global corporate AI investment, including mergers and acquisitions, minority stakes, private investments, and public offerings. Rapid growth in AI investment can indicate genuine innovation or speculative excess, depending on whether returns materialize.
metrics.explanation: Rapid growth can reflect either genuine innovation or speculative excess. Unsustainable acceleration may signal bubble formation.

metrics.label: Corporate Profits
metrics.description: in corporate profits with Inventory Valuation Adjustment (IVA) and Capital Consumption Adjustment (CCAdj). Change shows the percentage difference from a year ago.
metrics.disclaimer: This metric represents 'profits from current production' by removing distortions from inflation and accounting practices. IVA adjusts for the actual replacement cost of inventory, while CCAdj accounts for real equipment depreciation. This reveals the true health of corporate earnings. Unlike reported earnings-per-share (which can be inflated by buybacks or accounting methods), this tracks companies' fundamental ability to generate value. When these adjusted profits stagnate while stock prices rise, it often signals market overvaluation.
metrics.explanation: Stagnant or declining profits alongside rising stock prices can indicate overvaluation and disconnection from fundamentals.
metrics.dataSource: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, Corporate Profits with Inventory Valuation Adjustment (IVA) and Capital Consumption Adjustment (CCAdj) [CPROFIT], retrieved from FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis; https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPROFIT

metrics.label: Magnificent 7
metrics.description: of the S&P 500's total market capitalization is concentrated in the Magnificent 7 companies: Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Nvidia, Meta, and Tesla. Change shows the percentage point difference from a year ago.
metrics.disclaimer: The 'Magnificent Seven' term was coined by Bank of America's Michael Hartnett in 2023 to describe the tech giants driving market performance. This metric measures market concentration - when a small number of companies represent a disproportionate share of the index. High concentration means the broader market's health depends heavily on just seven firms rather than hundreds of others, increasing systemic risk if these companies underperform.
metrics.explanation: Higher concentration increases systemic risk and market vulnerability. Extreme levels have historically preceded corrections.
metrics.dataSource: Calculated from data available at https://www.slickcharts.com/sp500 and https://www.fool.com/research/magnificent-seven-sp-500/

groups.title: Infrastructure & Real World Friction
groups.description: Physical constraints and economic reality check.

metrics.label: RAM Prices
metrics.description: average consumer price for DDR4 16GB (2x8GB) 3200MHz RAM. Change shows the percentage difference from a year ago.
metrics.disclaimer: RAM prices serve as a proxy for AI infrastructure demand. As AI workloads require substantial memory capacity, rising RAM prices can indicate increased competition for computing resources driven by AI development and deployment.
metrics.explanation: Rising prices can signal increased AI infrastructure demand. Sharp or sustained increases may reflect speculative overinvestment.

metrics.label: Job Cuts
metrics.description: jobs cut in the US last month due to AI, according to Challenger, Gray & Christmas. In 2025, total AI-related job cuts reached 54,836. Change shows the difference from the previous month.
metrics.disclaimer: This metric tracks monthly U.S. job cuts where companies explicitly cited AI as the reason. While AI adoption can improve productivity, rising job displacement may signal economic disruption or companies over-investing in automation during a hype cycle.
metrics.explanation: Accelerating job cuts can indicate aggressive AI adoption. Rapid increases may suggest companies are over-investing in automation during a hype cycle.

groups.title: Retail Euphoria / Sentiment
groups.description: Tracking public perception and speculative behavior.

metrics.label: Berkshire Hathaway Cash-to-Assets Ratio
metrics.description: of Berkshire Hathaway's total assets last quarter were held in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term U.S. Treasury Bills. Change shows the percentage point difference from a year ago.
metrics.disclaimer: This ratio shows what portion of Berkshire Hathaway's assets Warren Buffett holds in cash versus investments. A rising ratio typically indicates Buffett finds few attractively priced opportunities - often a sign of overvalued markets or bubble conditions. High cash levels serve as a defensive strategy, preserving capital to deploy when prices correct. Conversely, a falling ratio suggests active deployment of cash into investments Buffett considers fairly valued. Essentially, this tracks whether one of history's most successful investors is prioritizing safety or growth opportunities.
metrics.explanation: A rising ratio can suggest limited attractive investment opportunities. High levels may indicate defensive positioning amid perceived overvaluation.
